chunks: And the acknowledgment that prayer is the pillar of the religion, and that it is the first thing the servant will be reckoned for on the Day of Resurrection among his deeds, and the first thing the servant will be asked about after the recognition. So if it is accepted, what is apart from it is also accepted, and if it is rejected, what is apart from it is also rejected.

And that the obligatory prayers in the day and night are five prayers, and they are seventeen units: Zuhr is four units, Asr is four units, Maghrib is three units, the final Isha is four units, and the morning (Fajr) is two units.

key_terms.الصلاة: Salat (ritual prayer) - the obligatory daily worship in Islam, considered the pillar of religion
key_terms.المعرفة: Al-Ma'rifa (recognition/knowledge) - refers to the recognition of God, His Prophet, and the Imams as proper beliefs
key_terms.المفروضات: Obligatory (fard) prayers - the five daily prayers mandated upon every Muslim
key_terms.عمود الدين: Pillar of the religion - a well-known description emphasizing prayer's central role

ai.seo_question: What are the five daily obligatory prayers and their units (rak'at) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This passage is from a creedal statement recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in al-Amali, delivered during a Friday assembly in Sha'ban 368 AH. It establishes that prayer (salat) is the foundational pillar of religion and the very first deed for which a servant will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment, even before other acts. The acceptance or rejection of all other deeds hinges upon the acceptance of one's prayer. It then specifies the five daily obligatory prayers totaling seventeen units (rak'at), a defining feature of Shia jurisprudence.

en.bilal-muhammad: It is the confirmation that the prayer is a pillar of the religion, and that it is first of what the servant will be reckoned by of his acts on the Day of the Resurrection, and the first of what the servant will be asked about after the recognition (al-ma`rifa) (i.e. of proper beliefs). So, if it is accepted, what is apart from it is [also] accepted, and if it is rejected, what is apart from it is [also] rejected.

The obligation of the prayers in the day and night are five prayers, and they are seventeen units: Thuhr is four units, `Asr is four units, Maghrib is three units, the final `Isha is four units, and the morning (al-ghada i.e. Fajr) is two units.
